samples.question: The picture is one chart panel crossed by nine pale vertical gridlines and by one black dashed horizontal line. Five traces run across the panel: one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one grey. The grey trace is a distractor and carries no information; ignore it completely. Every trace is a straight path from one gridline vertex to the next, so a trace's highest point is always one of its nine vertices. A coloured trace QUALIFIES when its highest vertex lies above the black dashed line; a coloured trace whose highest vertex lies below the dashed line does not qualify, no matter how far left or how high its other vertices are. Among the qualifying coloured traces only, take the one whose highest vertex sits furthest to the LEFT. In every picture at least two coloured traces qualify, no two coloured traces have their highest vertex on the same gridline, each coloured trace has exactly one highest vertex, and no vertex touches the dashed line. The colours, the drawing order and the left-hand starting heights carry no information; the answer need not be the tallest trace, need not be the trace whose highest vertex is furthest left overall, and the grey trace is never the answer. Which coloured trace has the leftmost highest vertex among the traces that qualify? Answer red, green, blue or orange.
